author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can browse a read-only specialty directory listing the veterinarians holding each specialty
summary: A read-only page presents the inverse of the veterinarian directory: every specialty by its stored name with the veterinarians who hold it, veterinarians holding none grouped separately, all on one page.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it shown by full name in first-name-then-last-name order
Given a specialty held by more than one veterinarian, when the directory is opened, then every veterinarian holding that specialty appears under it
Given a veterinarian who holds no specialty, when the directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under the grouping for holding none
Given the clinic's specialties, when the directory is opened, then all of them render on a single page with no pagination controls
Given the directory, when it is opened, then specialties and the veterinarians under each are presented in a stable order
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application stays out of scope (NG-2 unchanged)
notes: Product owner fixed the entry point as GET /specialties.html. The page is specialty-oriented, not the full veterinarian roster. NG-2 is explicitly unchanged; no new non-goal ADR.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory inverts the vet directory and reuses established patterns end to end: feature-package placement in vet/ (system-design Package Structure), direct controller->repository access with no service layer, server-rendered Thymeleaf, and the name-ordered lookup-enumeration pattern already realized by owner/PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes(). Specialty is a NamedEntity lookup structurally identical to PetType. The only additions are a SpecialtyRepository (mirroring PetTypeRepository), a SpecialtyController serving GET /specialties.html, and a specialtyList.html template; no new pattern, module, or integration shape. Recorded in system-design.md#contracts (new SpecialtyController and SpecialtyRepository rows). No ADR: straightforward, reversible, no trade-off (adr-template).
integration_points: New open GET /specialties.html route in the vet package (same trust profile as /vets.html; no inputs, no query params, no pagination)

SpecialtyController depends on SpecialtyRepository (enumerate all specialties in name order) AND VetRepository (all vets, cached) to invert the unidirectional Vet->Specialty mapping and derive the holds-none group
New template vets/specialtyList.html plus new message-bundle keys for the page heading and the holds-none grouping label in every locale (REQ-LANG-002 bundle-parity build test)

patterns.description: name-ordered lookup enumeration (@Query ... ORDER BY name); SpecialtyRepository mirrors it, uncached like PetTypeRepository
page-serving controller returning a vets/* view; SpecialtyController mirrors it
getNrOfSpecialties()==0 is the holds-none test the template already uses in vetList.html

risks.risk: Stable-order criterion: VetRepository.findAll() returns an unordered Collection, so vets under each specialty are not stably ordered by default
risks.mitigation: Sort vets explicitly in the controller (e.g. by lastName then firstName); specialties come pre-ordered from the repository's name-ordered query. Do not rely on DB/insertion order

risks.risk: 'every specialty the clinic knows' could be under-implemented by inverting only the specialties vets hold, dropping a specialty held by no vet
risks.mitigation: Enumerate from SpecialtyRepository as the source of truth (why SpecialtyRepository is warranted over vet-side-only access). Seed data holds all three specialties, so a vets-only shortcut passes current tests silently -- flag for reviewer

risks.risk: Holds-none grouping must appear only when at least one vet holds none (PRD non-functional #2)
risks.mitigation: Conditional render, mirroring vetList.html's nrOfSpecialties==0 guard

risks.risk: Hardcoded user-facing text would breach REQ-LANG-002 and fail the bundle-parity test
risks.mitigation: Add message keys for heading and holds-none label to all locale bundles under src/main/resources/messages/

notes: Controller placement (delegated to me; prd-entry file_targets flagged best-effort): dedicated SpecialtyController in the vet package, preserving the one-page-one-controller grain (Owner/Pet/Visit/Vet/Welcome/Crash). Adding the method to VetController is an acceptable lighter alternative -- either keeps placement in vet/. Test placement follows: SpecialtyControllerTests (not VetControllerTests as the prd-entry listed). SpecialtyRepository is warranted (not vet-side-only): honest read model for the specialty catalog, mirrors PetTypeRepository, uncached to avoid a new JCache region and the vet-cache invalidation open question (system-design Open Q #5). Controller-side inversion (Map<Specialty,List<Vet>> plus a no-specialty List<Vet>) follows the codebase's controller-holds-view-assembly reality; no new domain concept, so ubiquitous-language unchanged. NG-2 unchanged, no non-goal ADR (confirmed by prd-entry). IDE oracle not in this dispatch's toolset; covering-pattern claims confirmed by direct Read of PetTypeRepository, VetController, and Vet -- the weaker basis than symbol resolution. system-design.md edits: two #contracts rows added and the vet-package tree line pluralized; no ADR created.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: No injection surface: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() is a static parameterless JPQL query with a literal ORDER BY specialty.name; no user input reaches it, consistent with the codebase's parameterized-query mitigation.

No XSS: specialtyList.html renders all stored data (specialty names, vet first/last names) via auto-escaping th:text — no th:utext anywhere; string concatenation for vet full names stays inside th:text and is still HTML-escaped.

No new trust boundary: GET /specialties.html takes no request parameters, path variables, or body — nothing crosses an input boundary; it only inverts and re-renders the same vet/specialty data already exposed by the existing vet directory, so no incremental data exposure.
No supply-chain delta: build.gradle and other dependency descriptors are unchanged; no new dependencies to CVE-check.

Access-control posture unchanged: like every existing route the endpoint is unauthenticated by the app's documented design (system-design.md Security Context); this read-only public endpoint adds no privilege boundary and no sensitive data.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD REQ-SPEC-001 edge case 2 — 'The grouping for veterinarians holding no specialty appears only when at least one veterinarian holds none' — has no test. The template implements this with th:if="${not #lists.isEmpty(vetsWithoutSpecialty)}", but the setup always injects James Carter (no specialty), so the conditional is only exercised in the 'shown' direction. No test configures all vets with at least one specialty and verifies that the 'No specialties' row is absent. A regression removing the th:if guard would pass all 7 tests undetected.

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredName asserts radiology and surgery but omits dentistry. The name promises complete catalog coverage ('every specialty') but the assertions deliver only two of three. Dentistry is separately covered by test 6, which is correct, but test 1's name misleads future readers into thinking it is a complete catalog assertion. Either rename to theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtiesHeldByVeterinarians or add a dentistry containsString assertion to live up to the name.

approved_aspects: Discrimination test is valid: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyEvenWhenNoVeterinarianHoldsIt stubs findSpecialties() to return dentistry held by no vet; a vets-only implementation would never emit 'dentistry' in the response body and the test would fail — the risk flagged in the design-block is closed
BDD naming convention (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) followed consistently across all 7 tests
MockMvc used as the sanctioned web-layer harness; repositories mocked via @MockitoBean consistent with the @WebMvcTest slice and the existing codebase pattern (tolerated per brief)
Factory helpers specialty() and vet() wrap all domain-object construction, satisfying the factory-method rule

The vets-in-wrong-order setup (Ortega before Leary in findAll stub) actively exercises the controller's sort, making theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderVeterinariansStablyByLastNameThenFirstName meaningful rather than trivially passing
Five PRD acceptance criteria covered: stored-name listing, full-name format, multi-holder specialty, single-page no-pagination, stable vet ordering under each specialty

findings.description: Imports org.assertj.core.util.Lists and calls Lists.newArrayList() for a non-assertion purpose. List.of(rafael, helen, linda, james) serves the same purpose without the internal dependency.
findings.fix: Replace the Lists.newArrayList(...) call with List.of(rafael, helen, linda, james) and remove the org.assertj.core.util.Lists import.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Unchanged from the line-4 triage. This revision only resolves the doc-reviewer critical finding at docs/system-design.md:106 (review-feedback line 14): removed the literal URL 'at /specialties.html' from the SpecialtyController purpose column so the row describes route behavior only, consistent with the VetController row (line 105) and every other controller row in the #contracts table. The route value now lives solely in the @GetMapping source that the row's source pointer already carries.
notes: Finding accepted, not contested. My triage deliberately recorded the URL to pin the route contract, but the reviewer is correct that the #contracts table's own convention (VetController and all other rows) keeps route literals out of the purpose column and lets the source pointer carry them; mirroring a source constant in the table is the prohibited constant-literal pattern and would drift silently if the mapping changes. No separate durable home for the URL is warranted in system-design.md: the doc intentionally documents route behavior, not literal paths, so GET /specialties.html stays authoritative in the @GetMapping annotation. The product owner's verbatim 'GET /specialties.html' request is satisfied by the implemented route and its source pointer, not by a doc literal. Only the docs/system-design.md:106 finding is mine; the docs/prd.md sentence-length autofixes on line 14 go to product-requirements-expert in parallel.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: PRD edge case 1 (REQ-SPEC-001) covers both specialty ordering and veterinarian ordering. The veterinarian-ordering half is tested by theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderVeterinariansStablyByLastNameThenFirstName, which deliberately seeds Ortega before Leary and asserts Leary appears first. The specialty-ordering half has no analogous test. The setup stubs findSpecialties() to return dentistry, radiology, surgery in alphabetical order, but no assertion verifies they appear in that order in the rendered output. A controller that iterated them arbitrarily (for example by iterating a HashMap keyed by specialty) would pass all eight existing tests. A test modelled on the vet-ordering test — asserting indexOf(dentistry) < indexOf(radiology) and indexOf(radiology) < indexOf(surgery) in the response body — would catch any regression in passthrough ordering.

approved_aspects: Round-one finding 1 resolved: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitTheNoSpecialtyGroupingWhenEveryVeterinarianHoldsOne stubs vets.findAll() to return only specialty-holding vets and asserts not(containsString("No specialties")). The test discriminates: removing the th:if guard from the template would cause the No specialties row to render unconditionally, making the assertion fail. The fix is genuine.

Round-one finding 2 resolved: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyByStoredName now asserts all three catalog names (dentistry, radiology, surgery). All three stubs are verified end-to-end through the rendered HTML.

SpecialtyController line coverage is 100% (25/25 lines); SpecialtyDirectoryEntry record is 100% (1/1 line); Vet and Specialty are 100%. Pre-existing VetController (0%) and Vets (0%) drag the vet package total to 63.8%, but neither is part of this slice.
All eight tests follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} BDD naming school.
Factory methods specialty() and vet() wrap construction, eliminating bare constructor calls from test bodies.
The @BeforeEach comment explaining findAll() seeding order is load-bearing design context, not narration.
List.of(...) replaces the dropped org.assertj.core.util.Lists import, consistent with the code-quality finding applied between rounds.
MockitoBean stubs target VetRepository and SpecialtyRepository at the Spring Data boundary, which the brief tolerates for existing suite patterns.
theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyEvenWhenNoVeterinarianHoldsIt covers the catalog-as-source-of-truth invariant (dentistry held by no vet but returned by findSpecialties still appears).
PRD edge case 2 now has a dedicated, discriminating test.
